title: Migrating Legacy Ruby Applications
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of migrating legacy ruby applications in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply migrating legacy ruby applications in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to regression testing and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Migrating Legacy Ruby Applications through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding migrating legacy ruby applications helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Migrating Legacy Ruby Applications helps you reason about identifying deprecated and removed features. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Identifying deprecated and removed features. Then connect it to Updating dependencies. The remaining syllabus points—Incremental migration strategies, Regression testing—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Migrating Legacy Ruby Applications
content_blocks.code:
minimum_supported = Gem::Version.new("3.2")
current = Gem::Version.new(RUBY_VERSION)
puts(current >= minimum_supported)

items.title: Assuming the happy path is enough
items.text: Test an empty value, a boundary value, and one invalid value before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Treating an example as a universal rule
items.text: Check Ruby version, runtime implementation, and third-party library documentation when behavior is version-sensitive.

items.title: Mixing too many concerns
items.text: Separate input parsing, domain behavior, and output so each piece is easier to test.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports migrating legacy ruby applications. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain migrating legacy ruby applications, identify its place in ruby internals, native extensions, and legacy maintenance, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
